name: clarifydoc-vscode
description: Trace any button click to the API it calls and the table it writes. Call traces, blast radius and a code map for Copilot & Claude. 60+ languages, 100% local.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: ClarifyDoc runs a bundled analyzer process, and writes its analysis into the project. Both are blocked until you trust the workspace; in restricted mode the analysis goes to private storage instead.

virtualWorkspaces.description: ClarifyDoc analyzes files on disk and cannot run in a virtual workspace.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with ClarifyDoc
walkthroughs.description: Trace screens → API → database straight from your code. Static analysis, runs locally, nothing extra to install.

steps.title: Analyze your workspace
steps.description:
ClarifyDoc parses your code with tree-sitter and builds a map of routes, screens, data access and more.
[Analyze Workspace](command:clarifydoc.analyze)

media.altText: The report overview after an analysis: routes, screens, data and health at a glance

steps.title: Open the interactive report
steps.description:
Explore screens, call traces, architecture, the data model and health in an interactive report.
[Open Report](command:clarifydoc.openReport)

media.altText: Data flows: each screen and route traced to the tables it reads and writes

steps.title: Navigate from a screen to its data
steps.description:
Go to Definition (F12) on an API call opens the backend route that serves it. On a route, Find References lists the calls that reach it, and its CodeLens names the screens above and the tables below. Right-click any file → **ClarifyDoc** to open the report on it.
[Go to a Route, Screen or Finding](command:clarifydoc.goto)

media.altText: Call traces from a click to the database

steps.title: Let your AI agent read the map
steps.description:
ClarifyDoc publishes the analysis over MCP, so Copilot agent mode (VS Code 1.101+) can ask for routes, call traces, blast radius and the data model — no setup. For Claude Code, Cursor or Windsurf, one command writes their config for you.
[Set Up MCP for an AI Agent](command:clarifydoc.installMcpServer)

media.altText: The architecture view an agent can query over MCP

steps.title: Tune it
steps.description:
Toggle diagnostics/CodeLens, enable analyze-on-change, or point at a custom analyzer.
[Open Settings](command:clarifydoc.openSettings)

media.altText: Health findings, also shown in the Problems panel

enumDescriptions: Write the analysis to `.clarifydoc/` in the project. The directory ignores itself, so it never shows up in git. AI agents and the `clarifydoc` CLI find it with no configuration.
Write the analysis to the extension's private global storage, leaving the project tree untouched. External agents then need the exact path (use "Set Up MCP for an AI Agent").
clarifydoc.storage.markdownDescription:
Where analysis artifacts (`project-summary.json`, `report.html`, per-file JSON) are written.

`workspace` puts them in `.clarifydoc/` inside the project — the same place `clarifydoc analyze` and `clarifydoc mcp` use by default, so any AI agent opened on the project finds the map with no setup, and a CLI run shares one copy and one incremental cache with this extension. A self-ignoring `.gitignore` is written into that directory, so nothing appears in `git status` and your own `.gitignore` is untouched.

Falls back to `global` automatically when the workspace is untrusted or not writable.

clarifydoc.cliPath.markdownDescription: Advanced. Override the bundled analyzer with your own. Accepts a `dist/cli.js` file (run with Node) or a `clarifydoc` binary. Leave empty to use the analyzer bundled inside the extension. May be absolute or relative to the extension directory.

clarifydoc.nodePath.markdownDescription: Path to the Node.js executable used to run the analyzer. Leave empty to use `node` from your `PATH`, falling back to VS Code's own runtime (Electron-as-Node) when no `node` is found — so analysis works even with no external Node installed.

clarifydoc.diagnostics.enabled.description: Surface analysis findings (security, complexity, layer violations) in the Problems panel.

enumDescriptions: Security findings, with their CWE and the routes that reach them
Functions at or above the complexity threshold
Imports that cross the layer order or a team rule
Unused exports and unreachable files, as faded text (off by default: every finding is an accusation)
API calls that reach no route, at the call — with the route that does serve the path, and a quick fix to open it
Request bodies that disagree with the route they reach: a required field not sent, an undeclared one sent, a wrong type

clarifydoc.diagnostics.include.description: Which finding categories to report as diagnostics.

clarifydoc.diagnostics.complexityThresho.description: Report functions whose cyclomatic complexity is at or above this value.

clarifydoc.codeLens.enabled.description: Show CodeLens above functions (callers/callees/complexity/traces), classes (references) and routes.

clarifydoc.hover.enabled.description: Show a ClarifyDoc hover card (complexity, callers/callees, findings) over analyzed symbols.

clarifydoc.crossTier.enabled.description: Navigate across tiers: Go to Definition on an API call opens the backend route that serves it, Find References on a route lists the calls that reach it, and a route's CodeLens and hover show its callers, the screens above them and the data it reads and writes.

clarifydoc.incremental.description: Reuse cached per-file analysis for files whose contents are unchanged (mtime + SHA-256). Much faster on re-runs.

clarifydoc.enableLsp.markdownDescription: Run the optional layer-2 LSP enhancement to resolve cross-file calls the text linker missed. **Requires Docker.** Off by default.

clarifydoc.editorLsp.enabled.markdownDescription: After each analysis, ask the language servers this editor already runs where the calls ClarifyDoc could not resolve lead, and add the unambiguous answers as layer-2 links — layer 2 without Docker. Only servers you have installed are asked; an answer naming two places is left out. Skipped while `#clarifydoc.enableLsp#` is on. Run it by hand with *ClarifyDoc: Resolve Calls with the Editor's Language Servers*.

clarifydoc.editorLsp.maxQueries.description: At most this many definition questions per pass over the editor's language servers (a pass also stops after two minutes).

clarifydoc.lspTimeout.description: LSP server startup timeout in milliseconds. 0 uses the CLI default. Only used when LSP is enabled.

clarifydoc.gitHistory.description: Collect git churn / hotspot history during analysis.

clarifydoc.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyze. 0 means unlimited.

clarifydoc.includeGlobs.description: Additional file glob patterns to include.

clarifydoc.excludeGlobs.description: Additional file glob patterns to exclude.

clarifydoc.openReportAfterAnalyze.description: Open the interactive report automatically after a successful analysis.

enumDescriptions: Show the report inside a VS Code editor tab (webview).
Open the report in your external web browser.
clarifydoc.reportLocation.description: Where to display the interactive report.

clarifydoc.analyzeOnSave.description: Re-analyze the workspace (incrementally) a few seconds after source files change on disk — saves, branch switches, generated files. Runs quietly in the status bar; an open report is refreshed, never opened.

clarifydoc.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Publish this workspace's analysis to AI agents over the **Model Context Protocol**, so chat/agent modes can query routes, call traces, blast radius and the data model instead of guessing. Requires VS Code 1.101 or newer; on older builds use the *Copy MCP Server Config* command instead. The server runs the bundled analyzer and reads only the analysis this extension already produced.

clarifydoc.mcp.allowAnalyze.markdownDescription: Let an agent trigger a re-analysis through the MCP server's `clarifydoc_analyze` tool. Off by default: this extension owns analysis runs. Even with it off an agent is never stuck — a project with no analysis at all is analyzed once, on demand, and a directory lock keeps that from colliding with a run started here or from the CLI.

scripts.build: npm run bundle && npm run vendor && node esbuild.mjs --production
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile
